newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TARTU BREWERY SEES 12 MLN KROONS PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: TARTU BREWERY SEES 12 MLN KROONS PROFIT.

text.p: Estonian beer maker Tartu Brewery, in which Finnish Olvi has a 15 percent stake, said on Tuesday it estimates its 1997 profit at 12 million kroons compared to 0.4 million kroons in 1996.
A company official also told Reuters that it estimated that its turnover would grow to 253 million kroons in 1997 compared to 174.2 million kroons last year.
Tartu Brewery's shareholders on Tuesday approved the 1996 economic results, but postponed a decision on a possible share issue.
"The decision on the share issue will be taken in September or October this year or in the first half of 1998," the official said.
The company has a share capital of 7.5 million kroons, of which some 85 percent is owned by Magnum Grupp, a conglomerate that is involved in various economic activities.
Tartu Brewery, the second biggest in Estonia after Saku, said earlier it also plans to list its shares on bourse after the issue.
